newsitem.title: UK: Euro life, pensions to expand market share - report.
newsitem.headline: Euro life, pensions to expand market share - report.

text.p: European life and pension assets could grow to $6,000 billion by 2002, management consultant Datamonitor said on Tuesday in its report "European Savings and Investments".
This would represent 40 percent of all investment assets in Europe and compares with a figure of $4,100 billion plus now and $2,200 billion in 1990.
"European investment patterns are changing; no longer are people content with simple deposit accounts; consumers are now demanding more sophisticated products with better returns," the report said.

Datamonitor said that both pensions and direct investment in equity markets will grow strongly, adding that total European savings and investments are expected to reach $14,000 billion by 2002, compared with $12,700 billion in 1996.
Britain, which accounted for almost 25 percent of European savings and investments in 1996, will retain its market lead, the report said.
The opportunity for cross-border activity will increase markedly if and when European Monetary Union goes ahead, it added.
